thread:
Alex Morgan: Heads up — postmortem shows a recurring S3-proxy timeout pattern that triggers cascading request spikes. We need concrete runbook edits, owners, and a short triage flow (3 steps) + clear escalation path.
Priya Shah: Agree. Runbook is too branching right now. Short sequence + exact commands would help. Can we add KV cache flush & verification?
Mateo Rivera: I can own the KV cache remediation and verification steps. ETA 2 weeks to deliver tests + docs. Need someone to draft the exact commands for the runbook.
Jordan Lee: I'll own the escalation matrix and oncall doc updates. Proposal: add a direct pager to infra after 3 retries/failures in the triage flow.
Sam Patel: Notes from incident: my usual quick checks —
```
# health check
curl -sS http://service.internal/_health | jq .
# check pods
kubectl get pods -n infra -l app=s3-proxy
# tail logs
kubectl logs -n infra deploy/s3-proxy -c proxy --tail=200
# run cache invalidate (use with caution)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.internal/cache/invalidate?prefix=objects/"
```
Also prefer `POST /cache/invalidate?prefix=` over FLUSHDB.
Alex Morgan: Good — include both safe read-only checks and a controlled invalidation path. Proposed triage sequence (to add verbatim to runbook):
1) Service health + quick metric sanity (no write ops)
2) Check S3-proxy metrics and pod state
3) If confirmed, perform controlled cache invalidate or warm cache; if unsuccessful escalate to infra oncall.
Lara Chen: I'll edit the runbook and add a short gating checklist + a small pre-flight smoke test. @ops-bot can you create a PR template for runbook changes?
ops-bot: PR created: https://git.redwood/infra/runbooks/pull/142 — please review.
Priya Shah: Assigning remediation tickets now: RV-2453 (KV-cache remediation) -> owner: Mateo Rivera, due: 2026-04-06; RV-2454 (Runbook rewrite + triage flow) -> owner: Lara Chen, due: 2026-04-01; RV-2455 (Escalation matrix update) -> owner: Jordan Lee, due: 2026-03-30.
Mateo Rivera: Ack — I'll add test steps and a local replay script. Quick repro hint: `make sim-load TARGET=s3-proxy RATE=200` to reproduce the spike in staging.
Jordan Lee: For escalation, propose: page infra oncall after either 3 S3 5xx in 5 minutes OR p99 latency > 2s for 3 consecutive minutes. Does that sound reasonable?
Sam Patel: :thumbsup: Yes. Also add dashboard tiles for `s3_proxy_5xx` and `proxy_pending_requests`.
Alex Morgan: Timeline: runbook PR in 1 week, remediation tickets triaged daily until closed, follow-up review in 3 weeks (2026-04-15) during the incidents sync. I'll schedule the calendar invite.
Lara Chen: I'll include explicit command snippets in the runbook, e.g.:
```
# basic health check
curl -sS http://service.internal/_health
# grep recent errors
kubectl exec -n infra deploy/s3-proxy -- /bin/sh -c "grep ERROR /var/log/proxy.log | tail -n 50"
```
Priya Shah: Also flagging recurring pattern: most spikes correlate with rollout traffic ramps. Add a post-rollout canary check: run `make smoke` against canary and ensure `s3_proxy_5xx` remains low for 30m before promoting.
Jordan Lee: I'll add an automatic rollback rule for Dedicated rollouts: on sustained 5xx spike during rollout, trigger rollback after 2 consecutive failures and open incident.
Alex Morgan: Great. Next steps: Lara and Mateo to open PRs for runbook + remediation docs; Jordan to update escalation; Priya to track tickets. cc @incident-bot please create a follow-up reminder in three weeks.
incident-bot: Follow-up created: Incident follow-up task scheduled for 2026-04-15.
Alex Morgan: Thanks everyone — reconvene if any PRs hit blockers.
